missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend iron from fatigue alone; clarify laboratory status, current products, pregnancy and possible blood loss.
safety_exclusions: Fatigue alone does not diagnose iron deficiency or anemia.
Do not add iron to existing therapeutic or prenatal products without review.
Do not assume bisglycinate is appropriate without an indication.
professional_escalation_conditions: Shortness of breath, chest pain, syncope, significant bleeding, pregnancy, abnormal CBC/ferritin or suspected iron overload.
population_and_context: People reporting fatigue without established iron deficiency; fatigue is nonspecific and iron bisglycinate is not exempt from diagnostic requirements.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Iron supplementation for deficiency should follow diagnosis and clinician-directed treatment.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Iron fact sheet provides deficiency and reference information; symptoms alone are insufficient for diagnosis. This justification remains draft pending source passage verification, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional review.
